Another strong review, and it's right about the thing that matters most: **coverage**. Sixteen well-formed criteria don't help if four user scenarios (US3/US5/US7/US8) have no SC and nothing loops back to *why the scope exists* (H1/H2 closed). I accept the entire review — all 13 additions and all 6 wording fixes are **IN**. Traceability is non-negotiable for a control scope: every US and every FR must have a success criterion, or the scope can be "done" while the problem statement is still true on paper.

## All IN

- **SC-17** (re-run compliance-scan, H1/H2 no longer High, tasks closed, risk register updated) — the **loop-back**, the single most important omission. Without it, "done" doesn't mean the problem is solved.
- **SC-18** (negative test: dump + .env + bucket → no plaintext for someone without Vault) — the H1 proof in one line; a *different* claim from SC-01–03.
- **SC-19** (decrypt-verify sample, zero mismatches) — correctness vs coverage; a count of zero can't catch a wrong-codec or double-encryption bug.
- **SC-20/21/22/23** — close the US3 / US5 / US7 / US8 gaps respectively.
- **SC-24** (Vault stopped mid-run) — tests the load-bearing envelope property that was asserted everywhere and proven nowhere.
- **SC-25** (Vault hardening from config export), **SC-26** (network plane in ADR), **SC-27** (cutover residue), **SC-28** (trigger/owner/legal-hold/cert renewal), **SC-29** (single-node acceptance + M8 doc reconciliation + SaaS-cost) — all IN.
- **The `Evidence | Verified by (≠ executor)` column** — IN, and it's the sharpest structural point: *"the operator ran the rotation and the operator confirmed it"* is exactly the H7 SoD finding. A drill's verifier must not be its executor.

Wording fixes all IN: SC-07 (real **prod** sweep + **dev** kill-resume, both stated; escrow destruction date = last pre-rotation backup expiry), SC-12 ("locked 35 days, then lifecycle-expired" — kills the WORM-vs-deletable contradiction), SC-13 (name the 3 endpoints + dated baseline artifact), SC-01 ("attested per developer, signed"), SC-11 (RTO/RPO measured within FR-011 targets).

## Two refinements of my own

1. **Name the independent verifier, or `≠ executor` becomes unmeetable on a 3-person team.** The rule is correct, but for operator-run drills (SC-07, SC-21) on a small DDES team the verifier has to be a *named* someone. Cleanest fit: the **Key-holders** (the Operator/Key-holder split from 4.7) serve as independent verifiers of operator-run drills — they're already trusted, already distinct people, and this gives the key-holder role a second real duty. I'll note that against the column so it's not an abstract ideal.

2. **SC-19 should use a keyed hash (HMAC), not a bare hash.** Hashing health-PII plaintext to compare pre/post rotation is right, but a bare hash of a short, low-entropy value (a medical condition, a licence number) is a guessing oracle — the verification artifact would itself leak. Use an HMAC under an **ephemeral per-run key discarded at reconciliation**. Same proof, no plaintext-recovery side-channel on the most sensitive columns. I'll fold that into SC-19.

## Scale note

Section 5 goes from 16 → **29 SCs plus a verifier column**. That's a lot — but for a scope spanning 4 compliance frameworks, 8 drills, and 17 FRs, every criterion maps to a US/FR/control, so I'm not trimming. The density *is* the audit evidence.

> Here is my thoughts

> the thirteen constraints are the right kind — architectural guardrails, not restated requirements — and C13 in particular will save you a migration. What’s missing is mostly the operational and cryptographic guardrails that assessors read first, plus a handful of non-goals that will otherwise come up as “why didn’t you…” questions in a security questionnaire. Also D5 doesn’t need to stay parked; a default custody model is below.
> 
> Constraints missing
> 
> Operational
> 
> Change control on live data. Alpha runs on real production data. Cutover and the v1→v2 sweep are prod changes to every encrypted value in the platform. Constraint: announced maintenance window, written go/no-go checklist, abort criteria, rollback window (FR-005) — and check the ToS for a maintenance-notice obligation to Alpha participants.
> Dev/prod separation. Dev never touches the prod Vault, KEK, AppRoles or DB creds; dev Vault is dev-mode and throwaway. Implied by 4.2, stated nowhere as a rule.
> Executor ≠ verifier. Every drill record is signed off by someone other than the person who ran it. This came out of the SC review; it belongs here as a standing constraint, because it’s the SoD finding H7 is literally about.
> 
> Security hygiene
> 
> Secret-free telemetry. No key material, Vault token, secret-id, Shamir share or age key in any log, SCOPE-011 event, error message, health payload or crash dump. Rule 31 (assertNoSecrets at event choke-points) already exists — extend it to the new emitters in C3. C3 says every key op emits an event; this says what the event may not contain.
> No secrets in the repo. C8 puts Vault config in the app repo; it must say that config contains no secret-ids, tokens or shares, with WP-11 secret-scanning as the guard. Config-as-code and secrets-in-git are one careless commit apart.
> No new public surface. /internal/keyhealth authenticated; Vault firewall-closed; no public endpoint added by this scope. Stated in 4.4, not as a constraint.
> Cryptographic standards. AES-256-GCM with random 96-bit IVs; Transit aes256-gcm96; keys exportable=false; DEK plaintext never persisted to disk, DB or log; no algorithm or TLS-version downgrade path. One constraint, so no future change can quietly weaken it.
> 
> Design
> 
> Extensible envelope header. You’re changing the field-crypto envelope anyway. Reserve room for a key-id alongside the version so per-tenant keys / BYOK later don’t need a second migration. One byte of foresight now; a full sweep avoided later. (Per-tenant keys themselves stay a non-goal — see below.)
> Licence and software origin. Vault Community is BSL 1.1; our use (internal secrets management for our own SaaS) is within the grant; version pinned; upgrades via PR with a snapshot taken first. And an honest line for the ADR: the Vault binary originates from a US vendor — software origin isn’t data residency, but say it before an assessor does.
> Separate Onidel service for audit/snapshots. Onidel’s KB says access keys are issued per service, recommends one key pair per application, and lists no IAM-style policies. So “write-only credential” may not be achievable per bucket. Put the WORM buckets in a separate Onidel service from the documents bucket, with their own keys. WORM then protects against deletion; separation protects against the document credential ever reaching the evidence store.
> Dependencies — add, refine, unpark
> Add D7 — Vault VPS provisioned on Conetix, same DC as the app host (a VLAN needs that), with the cost line in GOD-SaaS-Cost.md. D1 covers the network, not the host.
> Add D8 — ToS maintenance-notice clause reviewed, window scheduled to comply.
> Add D9 — Key-holder availability scheduled for the three drills that need them (unseal, rekey on prod, restore). D6 names the people; this books their time.
> Reword D3. 003 and 014 are already version-aware (keyversion column; version in blob header). The gap is multi-version reads during the dual-key window and writes under the current version — a keymap, not a version tag.
> D5 — unpark it with a default. Two artefacts, five Shamir shares, one age private key:
> Shares 1–3: Andrew, Scott, Greg, each in their own MFA-protected password manager (not email, not a shared drive).
> Shares 4–5: printed, in tamper-evident sealed envelopes, held by two different external custodians (e.g. solicitor and accountant, or solicitor and a bank safe-deposit box). Different custodians is the point — if both envelopes sit in one safe, one person with safe access plus their own share can unseal alone.
> Age private key: one copy in each sealed envelope. It’s useless without the audit files, and it’s needed when Vault is down, so it must not live only in Vault or only with one person.
> Custody log (who holds what, since when), and an annual seal-intact check recorded as evidence. Leaver = rekey (FR-009) + re-issue envelopes.
> That’s a complete model you can accept or amend, rather than a parked item that holds go-live.
> Non-goals to add
> 
> These are the questions a procurement security questionnaire will ask; naming them now with a reason is cheaper than answering them cold:
> 
> N8 Auto-unseal — rejected on residency (every backend is a cloud KMS); revisit in SCOPE-035. Section 1 made this call; the non-goals list should carry it.
> N9 Per-tenant keys / BYOK / HSM — not this scope; envelope header reserves room (constraint above).
> N10 Dynamic database credentials (Vault database secrets engine) — static creds in Vault now; dynamic is the named follow-on.
> N11 mTLS client-cert auth to Postgres — follow-on once PKI is in.
> N12 Migration of Twilio / SMTP / push / signed-URL / session secrets — target this interface, land with their own WPs (name them).
> N13 Terraform — reviewed scripts at Alpha; Terraform at Beta (so nobody builds both).
> Wording

For a team this size that's the right trade (availability over internal-collusion defence), but it should be written into the C11 risk acceptance as a *conscious* choice, not left implicit — an assessor will ask "can any subset unseal alone?" and the honest, pre-written answer is "yes, the three internal holders, by design, for operational availability." **15:53 — Claude:**

Found it. **Every scraping job on production fails because the API container has no Chrome browser installed.**

**What happens:** the RitchieSpecs scraper runs a real browser through Playwright. When a job starts, its first step, `chromium.launch()`, fails immediately with:

> `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234/…`

The job is then marked failed before it fetches a single page.

**Why:**
- [deploy/Dockerfile.api](../proactive-by-ddes/deploy/Dockerfile.api) builds from the slim Node base and runs only `npm ci`.
- Playwright 1.62 no longer downloads browsers when it's installed, so the library is in the image but Chrome isn't. I confirmed inside the running production container that the browser folder doesn't exist.
- The container is also missing the operating-system libraries Chrome needs (`libnss3`, `libatk`, `libgbm`), so installing only the browser wouldn't be enough.
- It works on your Mac because Chrome was installed there separately. The dev server uses the same Dockerfile, so scraping almost certainly fails there too.

**The fix:** one line in `Dockerfile.api` after `npm ci`, which installs the headless browser and its system libraries, matched to the Playwright version:
```dockerfile
RUN npx playwright install --with-deps --only-shell chromium
```
It adds about 200–300 MB to the image. I'd also give the API container more shared memory in the compose file (`shm_size: 1gb`), because Chrome can crash on Docker's default of 64 MB.

**How I'd roll it out, by our process:**
1. Log it as a WXKanban bug task under SCOPE-032.
2. Make the change on a branch and build the image locally to prove the browser launches.
3. PR into `dev`, deploy to the dev server, and run a real scraping job there.
4. Release it to production as v0.2.1 through the same `dev` → `main` → tag route as v0.2.0.

Shall I go ahead with steps 1–3? I'd stop before deploying anything to production.

I have what I need to frame the amendment. Here is Phase 1 of the buildscope interview (the problem and the key decisions), with my recommendations for you to confirm or override before I draft Section 1.

**Reuse check: extend SCOPE-032, not a new scope.** SCOPE-032 owns the ingestion engine, the source registry and the "Unknown equipment type" rule. A type mapping only makes sense per source, so it belongs there, as **SCOPE-032 Amendment A: Source type mapping**.

**Proposed problem statement:**
> DDES admins can't load most of the RitchieSpecs catalogue. The scraper only keeps a model whose RitchieSpecs type name exactly matches a DDES equipment type, and RitchieSpecs uses different words ("Hydraulic Excavator", "Motor Grader", "Crawler Tractor") from DDES's own list ("Excavator", "Grader", "Dozer"). Today only **2 of 44** RitchieSpecs types match. Every other model is fetched, fails with "Unknown equipment type", and the run spends hours scraping pages it then throws away. The only workaround is renaming DDES's own types to RitchieSpecs' vocabulary, which would break what tenants see.

**Four decisions, with my recommendations:**

1. **Map, ignore or undecided, per source.** Each RitchieSpecs type is in one of three states:
   - **Mapped** to a DDES type. Several RitchieSpecs types can map to one DDES type; for example, Hydraulic, Midi, Mini and Mobile Excavator all map to "Excavator".
   - **Ignored**, for types DDES doesn't care about (Combine, Baler, cranes). These are **skipped before their pages are fetched**, which cuts run time and the load on RitchieSpecs. The scraper knows each model's type from the sitemap before opening its page, so this costs nothing extra.
   - **Undecided.** These fail as now, with a clearer reason ("No mapping for RitchieSpecs type …"), and are listed so an admin can decide.

   Mappings are stored **per source**, because a future second source will use its own vocabulary.
2. **No hard-coded starting set.** Exact name matches map automatically, so today's two keep working. A DDES admin maps the rest once, on a new **Type mapping** tab of the existing Source Administration screen. A "Refresh types" button lists every type the source offers, with undecided types highlighted. Mapping about 40 types by hand takes minutes, and keeping it out of code means dev and prod can't drift.
3. **Re-processing reuses "Retry failed".** After mapping a type, the existing retry button (FR-007) re-runs just those failed models, so no new mechanism is needed.
4. **Duplicate detection uses the DDES type, not the RitchieSpecs one.** The check for "is this the same model?" (make, type and model) uses the mapped DDES type, so models from different sources line up, which is what FR-008 intends. Models already created are unaffected, because both existing ones are exact matches.

**A first-pass mapping, for your domain check.** This is data the admin enters, not code. It's here to test the three states against reality, and the ❓ items are domain calls I can't make for you:

| RitchieSpecs type(s) | → DDES type |
|---|---|
| Hydraulic / Midi / Mini / Mobile Excavator | Excavator |
| Crawler Tractor, Wheel Dozer | Dozer |
| Motor Grader | Grader |
| Compactor | Roller - Compactor |
| Elevating Motor Scraper | Elevating Scraper |
| Motor Scraper | Open Bowl Scraper **or** Twin Power Scraper ❓ |
| Skid Steer Loader, Multi Terrain Loader | Posi-Track - Skid Steer |
| Rock Truck | Rigid Dump Truck (RDT) |
| Crawler Loader | Loader |
| 2wd / 4wd / Mfwd / Utility Tractor | Tractor (Ag or Civil) |
| Telescopic Forklift | Telehandler - Manitou ❓ (the DDES type name contains a brand, so every make would be filed under Manitou) |
| Dump Truck / Truck Tractor | Tipper Truck - Truck & Dog / Float - Low Loader - Prime Move ❓ |
| Loader Backhoe, Shovel, Pipe Layer, Tool Carrier, cranes, lifts, farm implements | **Ignore**, or add new DDES types ❓ |

## 16:15 — Andrew

> I think we should match the RitchieSpecs types in the DDES Catagolue type what are your views around this approach

**16:15 — Claude:**

Before giving a view, I'll check one fact that decides it: what else in the app depends on the DDES equipment-type list. If prestart checklists, competencies or tenants' fleets are tied to it, renaming or splitting types affects far more than the catalogue.

<details><summary>Actions taken (2)</summary>

- 16:15 — Ran: Find tables referencing equipment types
- 16:15 — Ran: Identify which tables reference equipment types

</details>

**16:16 — Claude:**

It's a reasonable instinct, and it is the simplest option for the scraper. But the code shows it would cost more than it saves, because the equipment-type list isn't only a catalogue label.

**What depends on the DDES equipment types** (checked in the schema just now):
- **Catalogue models.** Every model belongs to one type, and every tenant's machine inherits its type through its model.
- **Prestart checklists.** SCOPE-015 has one master prestart template per equipment type (`prestarttemplates.equipmenttypeid`), and the type decides which safety checklist an operator gets.
- **Prestart change requests**, keyed by type as well.

**What adopting RitchieSpecs' types would do:**
1. **Split prestart.** "Excavator" would become Hydraulic, Midi, Mini and Mobile Excavator. Each needs its own prestart template, or machines of the new types have **no prestart checklist**. That breaks the safety feature, RED lock included, unless every split type gets a template, and existing machines would have to be moved onto the new types.
2. **Remove the Australian site words workers use.** RitchieSpecs is a US taxonomy, using "Crawler Tractor" for a dozer and "Rock Truck" for a rigid dump truck. The app is meant to read in plain words, and an operator looks for "Dozer".
3. **Leave a mixed list anyway.** RitchieSpecs has no Water Truck, Light Vehicle, Service Vehicle, Fuel Trailer, Light Tower, Genset or Float/Prime Mover, so DDES would keep those and end up with two vocabularies in one list.
4. **Tie your list to a third party.** If RitchieSpecs renames a type, your taxonomy and prestart templates have to change with it. A second source would bring its own names, and you'd need mapping regardless.

**My recommendation:**
- **Keep DDES types as the master list** that prestart, fleet and tenants use.
- **Map RitchieSpecs types onto them** (the approach above).
- **Save the RitchieSpecs type on each catalogue model as a detail.** For example, "Excavator" with a RitchieSpecs type of "Mini Excavator" keeps the finer granularity visible in the catalogue without touching prestart. It's one extra stored field and doesn't widen the scope.
- **Where RitchieSpecs has something DDES genuinely runs but has no type for**, such as Loader Backhoe or a generic Telehandler, **add it as a new DDES type**. That's normal list upkeep, including giving it a prestart template, and it fits alongside mapping. Exact name matches are picked up automatically.

So both approaches have a place: map by default, and add a matching DDES type only where you really need a new one.

Which do you want for Amendment A?
- **[M]** Map, plus save the RitchieSpecs type on each model (my recommendation)
- **[R]** Adopt RitchieSpecs types into the DDES list, accepting the prestart-template and machine re-typing work
- **[E]** Explain any of this further

**16:45 — Claude:**

The root cause turned out not to be MXGuardian itself, and that shapes the best path with Mailgun.

**Why email isn't arriving:**
- The app sends from `no-reply@ddes.app` through MXGuardian. MXGuardian accepts every message: dev has never recorded a failed send since SMTP was set up.
- The problem is **`ddes.app` has no SPF, DKIM or DMARC records**, so Gmail, Outlook and company filters have no way to confirm the mail is genuine. They reject it or file it as spam.
- **Switching to Mailgun only fixes this because Mailgun requires those DNS records** before it will send from your domain. The DNS records are the real fix.

The good news: **no code change is needed.** The app already sends over SMTP using settings in the Global Admin Portal, and it has a "Send test email" button. Mailgun supports SMTP with per-domain credentials, and port 587 upgrades to TLS ([Send via SMTP](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/sending-messages/send-smtp)). This is configuration only, which the spec-first rule exempts.

**Recommended setup:**

1. **Sending domain `mg.ddes.app`, a subdomain.** It's unused today and keeps email reputation separate from anything else on `ddes.app`. Emails can still come *from* `no-reply@ddes.app`, because a signature on the subdomain counts for the parent domain under DMARC's standard alignment.
2. **Region: EU.** This is my recommendation, and it's a decision for you. Mailgun only offers US and EU regions, with no Australian one, so recipient addresses and email content leave Australia either way. The EU region keeps message data in the EU, which fits your GDPR commitment better. **The region is chosen when the domain is created and can't be changed later.** For EU, the SMTP host is `smtp.eu.mailgun.org`; for US, it's `smtp.mailgun.org`. Third-party guides give the EU host ([Wodby](https://wodby.com/docs/2.0/providers/mailgun/), [Ghost forum](https://forum.ghost.org/t/ghost-and-mailgun-eu-gotcha/14321)), so confirm it in the Mailgun dashboard.
3. **DNS records at Conetix**, where `ddes.app`'s DNS is hosted (`ns1/ns2.conetix.com`). From [Mailgun's domain verification guide](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/domains/domains-verify):
   - `mg.ddes.app` TXT (SPF): `v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all`
   - DKIM TXT: the host and value shown in the Mailgun dashboard
   - `mg.ddes.app` MX: `10 mxa.mailgun.org` and `10 mxb.mailgun.org` (needed for bounce handling, and harmless because nothing else uses the subdomain)
   - Tracking CNAME: **skip it, and switch open/click tracking off.** App emails are plain text, and tracking pixels add a privacy question for nothing.
   - **Plus `_dmarc.ddes.app`** TXT: `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:<your address>`. This monitors only, so it can't block anything, and big providers increasingly expect it.
4. **SMTP credentials:** create one per environment in Mailgun (Domain settings → SMTP credentials), so dev and prod can be revoked separately. The password is shown only once.
5. **Switch dev first.** In the Global Admin Portal, set host `smtp.eu.mailgun.org`, port `587`, the Mailgun username and password, and From `no-reply@ddes.app`. Click "Send test email", then check the message's headers show SPF, DKIM and DMARC as **pass**. Then do the same on prod.

**What's yours to do:** create the Mailgun account and domain, add the DNS records in Conetix's DNS panel, and create the SMTP credentials.

**What I'll do:**
- Confirm the DNS records have propagated, before Mailgun finishes verifying.
- Check the test email's headers.
- Update the tech-stack and data-processing document to name Mailgun as the email provider. That item was marked "⚠ confirm which provider" in the document for your solicitor.
- Track the migration as a WXKanban task.

**Later, and not needed to fix delivery:** Mailgun can notify the app about bounces and spam complaints through webhooks, so admins would see "this email bounced" in the app. That's new app behaviour, so it would need a spec.

Two decisions before you start: **the EU region** and **`mg.ddes.app` as the sending domain.** Are both OK?

Sources:

- [Mailgun quickstart](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/quickstart)
- [Mailgun: Send via SMTP](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/sending-messages/send-smtp)
- [Mailgun: Domain verification](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/domains/domains-verify)

## 17:08 — Andrew

> Okay should we chain from SMTP to API using Mailgun or should be add the Mailgun API as an option I am looking for an opinion here

**17:09 — Claude:**

My opinion: **stay on SMTP, and don't add the Mailgun API now, either as a replacement or as an option.**

**Why SMTP is the right choice now:**
1. **It fixes the actual problem.** The missing SPF, DKIM and DMARC records are what's losing your mail. The API would deliver no better, because Mailgun signs and sends both the same way.
2. **No code.** SMTP is a settings change you can test with the existing "Send test email" button. Switching to the API, or adding it alongside, means new code, a new secret, tests, and a spec first under the spec-first rule.
3. **It keeps you portable.** You're moving providers right now, and with SMTP that's just changing a few settings. With the API built in, the next move means rewriting code.
4. **One sending path is easier to trust.** Offering both means two ways for email to break and two things to test on every change, and the option would rarely be used.

**What the API is usually chosen for, and why you don't need it:**
- **Seeing bounces and complaints in the app.** That comes from Mailgun **webhooks**, which fire for mail sent over SMTP too. The SMTP response also returns Mailgun's message ID, so a future webhook feature can still link each event to the right email.
- **Tagging and per-message data.** Mailgun accepts these as email headers over SMTP.
- **Batch sends and server-side templates.** Not needed for account and safety emails, where the app writes each message itself.

**What would change my mind:**
- **The new host blocks outgoing mail ports.** Some cloud providers block SMTP ports, while the API runs over normal HTTPS. Vultr currently allows port 2525 to MXGuardian, and we'll know about 587 from the first test email. Re-check at the Vultr → Conetix migration. If it's blocked, switch to the API at that point, replacing SMTP rather than adding a second path.
- **Volume growing into bulk sending**, such as large notification batches, where the API's batching earns its keep.

So: SMTP now, webhooks later if you want delivery visibility in the app, and the API only if a blocked port forces it. The two decisions from before still stand: the EU region and `mg.ddes.app` as the sending domain.

Here's what I found. It's a gap in the spec rather than a coding bug, and it's a real dead end.

**What's happening:**
- SCOPE-003 FR-010 only specifies **"Create and deactivate DDES_ADMIN accounts"**. The app was built exactly to that: the admin screen has a Deactivate button, and a deactivated row just shows the red "Deactivated" label with no actions.
- **It's worse than it looks.** "Create admin" refuses any email address that already exists ([admin.ts:39-40](../proactive-by-ddes/apps/api/src/services/admin.ts#L39-L40)). So a deactivated administrator can **never come back**, not even by re-creating them. If someone leaves and returns, or is deactivated by mistake, the only fix is a different email address.
- The spec also contradicts itself: FR-009 and FR-011 say the last admin "cannot be **deleted**", but nothing in the spec, and no feature, deletes an admin.

**My recommendation:**
1. **Add reactivation. Yes.** It's small (one service function, one route, one button and tests). On reactivation the person **must set a new password at next sign-in**, because the old one may be known to someone it shouldn't be. It's recorded in the audit trail, like create and deactivate.
2. **No "permanently delete" button.** I recommend against it for two reasons:
   - **82 database tables point at user records**, including hash-chained audit events and settings changes. Hard-deleting an admin would either fail or leave holes in the audit trail an assessor relies on.
   - **Your platform policy already covers removal**: deactivate, keep for 7 years, then hard-delete (SCOPE-012). A person's request to erase their data goes through SCOPE-012's erasure process, not a delete button.

   If the real concern is clutter on the list, a "Hide deactivated" toggle solves that cleanly. Say if you want it.
3. **Fix the "deleted" wording** in FR-009 and FR-011 to "deactivated".

**Proposed SCOPE-003 change**, shown as the full revised sections:

```
### FR-009 — Seed the first DDES_ADMIN (moved from SCOPE-007 FR-020)
- [ ] One DDES_ADMIN exists from deployment
- [ ] Its password is set at deployment, never fixed in code
- [ ] It is flagged for a forced password change at first sign-in (the change itself is SCOPE-002 FR-008)
- [ ] The account cannot be deactivated while it is the last active one (FR-011)

### FR-010 — Create, deactivate and reactivate DDES_ADMIN accounts (moved from SCOPE-007 FR-021)
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can create another DDES_ADMIN account
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can deactivate one; a deactivated account cannot sign in
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can reactivate a deactivated account; it can sign in again and must set a
      new password at its next sign-in
- [ ] Only a DDES_ADMIN can do any of these
- [ ] Each action is recorded (created / deactivated / reactivated)

### FR-011 — Never leave the platform unadministrable
- [ ] The last remaining active DDES_ADMIN cannot be deactivated
- [ ] The refusal explains why, in plain language
```

Added to **Out of Scope**:
```
- Permanently deleting a DDES_ADMIN account from the portal — accounts are deactivated, never
  deleted, so the audit trail stays intact; removal of personal data follows SCOPE-012 retention
  (7 years, then hard delete) and its erasure process
```

**17:51 — Claude:**

**Yes and no.** Self-service reset exists for everyone, but no admin can send a reset to another admin.

**What exists today:**
- **Self-service "Forgot your password?"** on the sign-in page (SCOPE-002 FR-005/006). It works for DDES administrators as well as tenant users: a single-use link valid for one hour, rate-limited and audited.
- **There's no "send a reset to this person" action.** An admin can't trigger a reset for another admin. Creating an admin also means typing a temporary password and passing it on yourself.

**My recommendation: add "Send password reset email" to the Administrators screen.** It reuses the existing reset email and link, so nothing new is invented, and it helps in three situations:
1. **An admin is locked out** and asks a colleague to help.
2. **Reactivation.** The person may have forgotten their old password, and the forced change at sign-in needs the old one to get in. Sending a reset link alongside fixes that.
3. **Safer onboarding.** After creating an admin, you can send them a link to set their own password, so nobody has to pass a password around.

The admin who triggers it never sees or sets the password, and it's recorded in the audit trail with who sent it.

**One dependency:** this is only useful once email actually arrives, so it depends on the Mailgun setup and the DNS records. Until then, reset emails (self-service included) may land in spam or not at all.

Here is the revised FR-010 in full, with this folded in. FR-009, FR-011 and the Out of Scope addition stay as I showed them before.

```
### FR-010 — Create, deactivate and reactivate DDES_ADMIN accounts; send a password reset
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can create another DDES_ADMIN account
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can deactivate one; a deactivated account cannot sign in
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can reactivate a deactivated account; it can sign in again and must set a
      new password at its next sign-in
- [ ] A DDES_ADMIN can send another active DDES_ADMIN a password-reset email — the same single-use,
      one-hour link and rate limits as the self-service reset (SCOPE-002 FR-005/006); the sender
      never sees or sets the password. Refused for a deactivated account (reactivate it first)
- [ ] Only a DDES_ADMIN can do any of these
- [ ] Each action is recorded, naming who did it (created / deactivated / reactivated /
      reset sent)
```

**18:47 — Claude:**

Mailgun is working: emails from `no-reply@post.ddes.app` are being delivered. Checking the DNS directly with Conetix's nameserver, though, the setup is only partly done.

**What's in place:** the **DKIM** record `smtp._domainkey.post.ddes.app` is published. Mailgun signs each email with it, and that signature is what's getting mail delivered now.

**What's missing:**

| Record | Where | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPF** (TXT) | `post.ddes.app` | `v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all` | Microsoft 365 and Outlook, common with construction businesses, weigh this heavily. Without it, more mail lands in junk. |
| **MX** (2 records) | `post.ddes.app` | Copy the exact two values from Mailgun's DNS page (EU domains use `mxa.eu.mailgun.org` / `mxb.eu.mailgun.org`) | Without them, Mailgun can't receive bounces, so invalid addresses go unnoticed. Some strict mail servers also reject mail from a domain with no mail records. |
| **DMARC** (TXT) | `_dmarc.ddes.app` | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:<an inbox you check>` | Gmail and Yahoo increasingly expect it. With `p=none` it only reports and never blocks. |

All three go in the Conetix DNS panel. Mailgun's domain page should then show every record as verified, and I'll re-check from outside once you've added them.

**Also outstanding:**
- **Dev hasn't been switched.** It still sends through MXGuardian from `no-reply@ddes.app`. I recommend a separate Mailgun SMTP credential for dev, entered in dev's Global Admin Portal settings, then "Send test email".
- **A failed email on dev was mine.** The one failure recorded today is the password reset my browser test sent to a fake `@proactive.test` address. It's not a problem.
- **Which region did you choose, EU or US?** I need it to update the tech-stack document for your solicitor, which currently says "⚠ confirm which provider". Mailgun becomes the named email processor, and their data processing agreement covers compliance finding M4.

**19:18 — Claude:**

The 11 **JS-0833** findings were DeepSource misreading the files, not bugs in them, so the fix is one line of config, merged into `dev` in [PR #66](https://github.com/Business-Momentum-Capital-Pty-Ltd/proactive-by-ddes-app/pull/66).

**What was happening:** every flagged file is a valid ES module. Seven are `.mjs` scripts and two are the web app's Tailwind and PostCSS configs. The repo's root `package.json` doesn't say which module type it uses, so DeepSource read the files as old-style CommonJS scripts and called every `import`/`export` a syntax error.

**The fix:** `.deepsource.toml` now sets `module_system = "es-modules"` explicitly for the JavaScript analyzer. I first checked there's no CommonJS anywhere in the repo, so this is correct for every file. I chose it over adding `"type": "module"` to the root `package.json`, which would also change how Node runs root-level files. The config file checks out as valid TOML, and no code changed.

DeepSource will confirm it on its next analysis of `dev`. If any of the 11 are still listed afterwards, the fallback is to set `"type": "module"` in the root `package.json`. That's safe, given there's no CommonJS.

Send the next batch when you're ready.

**19:21 — Claude:**

Yes. DeepSource has an official MCP server built for this, so once it's connected I can read the issue list myself instead of you pasting it.

**Setup:**

1. In a terminal (VS Code's own terminal works), run:
   ```bash
   claude mcp add --transport http -s user deepsource https://mcp.deepsource.com/mcp
   ```
   `-s user` makes it available in both your workspaces, the kit and the app repo. Use `-s project` if you'd rather it lived in one repo only.
2. Start a new Claude Code session, or run `/mcp`. The first time I use it, a browser window opens to sign in to DeepSource. No token to copy or store.
3. Tell me when it's connected and I'll check by listing the open issues for `proactive-by-ddes-app`.

I'd rather you run that command than me: it changes your Claude Code setup, and the sign-in has to happen in your browser anyway.

**What changes once it's connected:**
- I can pull the open issues directly, filtered by severity, type or file, and work through them in batches. The fixing process stays the same: branch, fix, test, PR into `dev`, and a WXKanban record.
- I can check whether DeepSource has actually cleared an issue after a fix merges. For example, I could confirm whether PR #66 cleared the 11 JS-0833 parsing errors, instead of assuming it did.
- The sign-in gives me the same DeepSource access you have, and the server can also change DeepSource settings. **I'll only read issues and results unless you ask for more.**

**If you'd rather not add an MCP server,** the DeepSource command-line tool does the same job with a personal access token (`deepsource auth login --with-token …`, then `deepsource issues --output json`). The MCP route is simpler because it needs no token handling.

| **Membership** | 3.5% | **56.5%** | Permissions only come from an active membership. A company can't remove its last admin or its last person who can manage members. Invitations expire and are stored securely |

**No bugs found.** I broke 9 rules on purpose and the tests caught every one, including letting a correction overwrite any field and letting erasure ignore a legal hold.

**Bugs found, logged in WXKanban and not fixed** (as agreed, these tests change no app code):
1. **Critical, security (task 56a1311b):** one company can read or change another company's CRM data:
   - A project can be linked to another company's client, and that client's name is then shown.
   - The contact role and unlink actions don't check the company, so they can delete another company's role assignments or take its Primary contact slot.
   - A client's parent can be another company's client, and its name is shown.
   - A client's owner isn't checked as a company member.

   Attempting it needs another company's record ID. The same code is almost certainly live in prod (v0.2.2).
2. **High, payroll and rostering (task 4d0fee68):**
   - Correcting a time entry doesn't recalculate the timesheet, so the payroll export can show the new times with the old hours.
   - Deleted time entries can still be exported.
   - Publishing a roster turns shifts the worker has already confirmed back into plain "published" ones, and sends them the notice again.
   - An edited shift's hours are counted twice.
   - Leave that starts the next day is wrongly flagged as a clash.
   - Two workers' offline clock-ins can collide, and one is silently dropped.
3. **High, prestart templates (task 992f26ab):** publishing a new version never retires the old one. Live prestarts still pick the newest version, so this is a record problem, not a safety one.
4. **Medium, maintenance and catalogue (task e5459ece):**
   - A rejected service point is still partly saved.
   - A value can't be cleared once set.
   - A model or equipment type can be saved with a blank name.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Supervisor approval:** should a supervisor be able to approve a timesheet that still has unresolved exceptions? The code comment says yes; the spec wording says no.
- **Rejected template drafts:** should a rejected prestart template draft be revisable and resubmitted, or closed for good?

**Recommendation:** fix the CRM security bug next, before the second wave of tests. It's a small fix in one PR, using company checks that already exist in the same files. Then ship it in a release, because prod is affected. Shall I go ahead?

**06:05 — Claude:**

Confirmed: DeepSource never analysed main's commit (945c7f4). Checking what ignore options DeepSource offers before I recommend a fix:

**06:05 — Claude:**

Nothing broke in 263da2d. DeepSource's own analysis of that commit on dev found **0 new issues**.

The 507 "new" issues come from a second analysis DeepSource ran on the same commit for **PR #77** (dev → main). For a PR, it compares against the target branch, which here is main at v0.2.2 (945c7f4). DeepSource has **never analysed main**; it only analyses dev, its default branch, and pull requests. With nothing on record for main, everything in every file the release touched shows up as new, including issues that were already there. For example, the flag on `clients.ts:58` is on a line that was already on main and that I didn't change. Every future dev → main release PR will look like this.

What the 507 are:

| | Count | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| Test-file style rules | Most of the ~428 JavaScript issues | Spread across the ~30 new test files: short names like `m` and `f` (JS-C1002), `!` assertions (JS-0339), empty mock functions (JS-0321), and async mocks with no `await` (JS-0116). These are normal in tests. |
| Older issues in app files the release touched | The rest of the JavaScript issues | For example `!` assertions in `clients.ts`, `contacts.ts` and `projects.ts`. They aren't new, just surfaced because those files changed. |
| Coverage (TCV-001) | 79 | Almost all are untested lines in `ritchiespecs-connector.ts` (the scraper) and `minio.ts` (the S3 storage client). These came up only because the type clean-up touched those files; neither has tests yet. |
| Coverage on new code | 4 | All in `contacts.ts`. Three lines are my fix's `unassociateProject` path, which the tests don't run all the way through. One is the "already the Primary" error message, which ties to the bug in task 118359a6. The odd one, line 46, is the small `listContactRoles` lookup. |

**What I'd do:**
1. **Stop the test-file noise.** Add DeepSource ignore rules for JS-C1002, JS-0339, JS-0321 and JS-0116 on test files only (`**/*.test.ts` and `**/test-support/**`). App code would still be checked for all four. You said earlier that ignoring DeepSource rules needs your OK, so I haven't done it.
2. **Cover the 4 new `contacts.ts` lines.** I'd do this together with the "already the Primary" fix from task 118359a6.
3. **Leave the scraper and S3 client coverage** for the second wave of tests, where they belong.
4. **Release PRs:** expect this result every time and judge each release by the dev analysis instead. The alternative is having DeepSource analyse main as well, which would roughly double its runs.

Shall I add the ignore rules in step 1 and do step 2?

## 08:01 — Andrew

> What is the best way to work on resolving the DeepSource issues for example 7056a88 has two issues Introduced so would it be best that we work through each group of identified issues one by one and then resolve any issues that get introduced

**08:01 — Claude:**

Yes. One group at a time, with every new issue fixed before moving on, is the right way to do it. It avoids two problems I ran into today: running six helpers in parallel made changes hard to check and costly to stop, and the two new issues slipped through because I wasn't checking DeepSource's result on each PR before merging.

**How each group would work:**
1. Pick one rule, or a few small related rules.
2. Fix it on its own branch.
3. Run the tests, type-checks and web build. For web changes, also compare screenshots of every screen before and after.
4. Open the PR and **wait for DeepSource's check on that PR**. It must show **0 new issues**, and the group's count must go down. If anything new appears, fix it on the same PR before merging.
5. Merge, then confirm the dev totals in DeepSource dropped as expected.
6. Move to the next group.

**Suggested order, lowest risk first:**

| # | Group | Count | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | The 3 introduced today: the false "secret" in `bootstrap.sh`, the long-form promise in `fake-db.ts`, and the second new issue on 7056a88 | 3 | none |
| 1 | Small rules: optional chains, string concatenation, regex `u` flag, `const`, `this`, labels and similar | ~30 | low |
| 2 | Shorthand coercions and template literals with nothing inside | ~120 | low |
| 3 | `void` → `runAsync` | 200 | low, mostly web |
| 4 | Short names | 306 | low |
| 5 | Empty functions | 146 | low |
| 6 | Unescaped characters in JSX text, `autoFocus` | ~100 | medium (web; screenshot check) |
| 7 | JSX nesting depth, over-complex functions | ~120 | highest (restructures screens; screenshot check per group) |
| — | The two decisions waiting on you: the `closeProject` route and `import * as schema` | 6 | — |
| — | Coverage (untested lines) | — | separate track, since it's fixed by writing tests |

**Two housekeeping steps:**
- I'd **discard the three half-finished workspaces** from the stopped work. Their changes were never reviewed, and redoing them group by group is cleaner than salvaging them.
- DeepSource can also block a PR that adds new issues, a setting called a "quality gate". With it on, an introduced issue can't be merged by accident. Turning it on changes your repository settings, so it needs your OK.

Shall I start with group 0, the three issues introduced today?

## 11:43 — Andrew

> Can you have a look at Deepsource and see why Test coverage is timing out and what do we need to fix on our end so that it doesn't time out

**11:43 — Claude:**

Looking at how coverage reaches DeepSource, starting with the CI workflow that uploads it:

<details><summary>Actions taken (3)</summary>

- 11:43 — Ran: Read coverage workflow and DeepSource config
- 11:43 — Ran: Check which commit the PR coverage upload used
- 11:43 — Ran: Read the coverage report step output

</details>

**11:43 — Claude:**

**Found it, and the fix is one line in our CI workflow.** DeepSource's own upload message says so:

> *"Artifact successfully uploaded … on commit **f4bc5c3**. Warning: Looks like the checkout step is making a merge commit. Test coverage Analyzer would not run for the reported artifact because the merge commit doesn't exist upstream."*

**What's happening:**
1. On a pull request, GitHub's checkout step doesn't check out the PR's own commit. It builds a temporary merge commit (for PR #94 that was **f4bc5c3**, made from the PR head 9e68f5d plus dev).
2. Our workflow runs the tests on that merge commit and uploads coverage labelled with **f4bc5c3**.
3. DeepSource waits for coverage for the PR's real commit, **9e68f5d**. That upload never arrives, so its test-coverage check sits on "pending" until it times out.

Pushes to dev aren't affected, because there's no merge commit there. That's why coverage on dev works.

**The fix** is in `.github/workflows/deepsource-coverage.yml`. Tell the checkout step to use the PR's own commit:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
```

On pull requests it checks out the PR's real commit. On pushes it falls back to the pushed commit, as now. This is the change DeepSource's documentation asks for: [Test coverage with GitHub Actions](https://docs.deepsource.com/docs/analyzers-test-coverage#with-github-actions).

**Nothing else is needed on our side.** The tests run and the upload succeeds; it's only labelled with the wrong commit.

**How I'd do it:** as its own small set, with a WXKanban task, a branch and a PR. That PR proves itself: if the fix works, DeepSource's test-coverage check on that PR should **finish** instead of sitting on pending, for the first time. Nothing merges until you OK it. Shall I go ahead?

There's one catch. Changing app code in a file makes DeepSource re-report every existing style issue in that file, which would fail its JavaScript check. So each fix PR would also clean up the other DeepSource findings in the file it touches, the same way we did for groups 1 and 2.

## 21:07 — Andrew

> What is The medical "outcome" question

**21:07 — Claude:**

It's about how a worker's medical self-declaration shows up on the member medical page.

**What happens now:**
- On "My tickets", the worker fills in a medical self-declaration. One question is "Fit for your work tasks?", a free-text box where they might type "Yes" or "Fit, but sore knee".
- When it's saved, the app also stores that answer in a field called **outcome**.
- The member medical page (the HSEQ view) shows that field as **"Clinician outcome"**. It colours it by guessing from the words: green unless the text contains "unfit" or "restrict".

**Why that's wrong:**
- A self-declaration is the worker's own statement, not a clinician's assessment. Clinician outcomes come from the separate fitness certificate, recorded with a fixed choice: Fit / Fit with restrictions / Unfit.
- So a worker typing "Yes" appears to HSEQ as a green **Clinician outcome: Yes**, which looks like a doctor cleared them.
- And a worker typing "not unfit" would show red, because it contains the word "unfit".

**My recommendation:** stop saving the self-declaration answer as the outcome. The answer is still kept as "task fitness", so nothing is lost. The "Clinician outcome" row then shows "—" for a self-declaration, and only a real clinician outcome appears there.

Since this changes what HSEQ sees about someone's fitness for work, it's your call. Shall I make that change?

## 21:07 — Andrew

> Should we have two buttons one for fit and the other for unfit

**21:08 — Claude:**

Yes, I'd recommend that, with one adjustment: label the answer as the worker's own, not as a clinician's.

1. **On the self-declaration form,** replace the free-text "Fit for your work tasks?" box with two buttons: **Fit for my work tasks** and **Not fit**. Keep the existing "Any treatment or restrictions?" box, so someone who is fit with a limitation can still say so.
2. **On the member medical page,** show the answer as **"Worker says: Fit"** or **"Worker says: Not fit"**. "Not fit" is shown in red so HSEQ notices it. The "Clinician outcome" row is then used only for a real clinician's fitness certificate.

This is better than free text because it's a clear answer that can be reported and filtered on. It also stops the page guessing from someone's words, and the worker's answer is never mistaken for a doctor's.

- **One decision for you:** when someone answers "Not fit", should anything happen beyond the red label, such as notifying HSEQ? If you're not sure, I'd start with just the red label and add a notification later if you want it.

Here's my draft of the spec change for your approval. I'll show each affected section in full, as it would read after the change. Nothing has been edited yet.

**SCOPE-010 · `specs/010-worker-competency-compliance/spec.md`**

### FR-008 — Medical (self-declaration + attachable clinician certificate)
- [ ] Every member completes a **self-declaration** at wizard step 4. It covers explicit consent, declared safety-relevant conditions, **fitness for their work tasks**, treatment/restrictions, attestation and date, and is recorded via `consentrecords`.
- [ ] **Fitness for work tasks is a fixed choice:** the worker taps one of two buttons, **"Fit for my work tasks"** or **"Not fit"**. It is required before the declaration can be submitted. A worker who is fit with a limitation chooses "Fit" and describes it under treatment/restrictions.
- [ ] The worker's answer is **their own statement, never a clinician outcome**. On the member medical view it shows as **"Worker says: Fit"** or **"Worker says: Not fit"**, with "Not fit" shown in red (icon + word, never colour alone). The self-declaration **does not set the clinician outcome**.
- [ ] Declarations made before this change keep their original free-text answer, shown as written under "Worker says", with no colour.
- [ ] The self-declaration is **fresh per membership** and **never portable**.
- [ ] A **clinician fitness certificate** may be attached as a credential (FR-004). It has:
  - a **fixed outcome** of exactly one of `fit` / `fit-with-restrictions` / `unfit`;
  - **restrictions captured as free text** (expected when the outcome is `fit-with-restrictions`);
  - a review/expiry date;
  - the assessing provider and a document.

  It is **optional**, required only when a tenant's matrix says so (FR-002). **Only this certificate's outcome appears as "Clinician outcome"** on the member medical view.
- [ ] Non-blocking. Neither answer is ever auto-decided, and a "Not fit" answer does not lock or block the worker; it is surfaced for a human (HSEQ) to act on.

**Data model (the `medicaldeclarations` line)**
`medicaldeclarations` (`usertenantid` — per-membership, not portable — responses, `taskfitness` (`fit` | `not_fit`; earlier declarations hold free text), `outcome` (no longer set by the self-declaration), `date`).

**Open Questions** (new resolved entry)
- ~~Should the self-declaration's task-fitness answer be free text, and may it appear as a clinician outcome?~~ **Resolved (2026-10-12, Andy):**
  - The answer is two buttons: Fit for my work tasks / Not fit.
  - It is shown as "Worker says", never as "Clinician outcome".
  - "Not fit" is shown in red, with no automatic notification for now.

**Design note** (`page-teamcompliance.md`, Member medical read)
- The read-only rows gain **"Worker says"**.
- **"Clinician outcome"** shows only a clinician certificate's outcome, and "—" otherwise.

**Things to check before you approve:**
- **"Not fit" behaviour:** I've written it as a red label only, with no notification to HSEQ, which was my suggested starting point. Say if you want a notification instead.
- **Button wording:** "Fit for my work tasks" / "Not fit". The form notes its wording is authored by DDES WHS, so they may want to word these.
- **Earlier declarations:** existing free-text answers stay as written and aren't converted, so no health data is changed.

Approve as written, or tell me what to change? Once approved, I'll save it to the spec and WXKanban, then build it as its own small PR.

I've opened the hotfix for the account-takeover hole as [PR #113](https://github.com/Business-Momentum-Capital-Pty-Ltd/proactive-by-ddes-app/pull/113) into `main`. It isn't merged or deployed yet, so the hole is still open on proactive.ddes.app until v0.2.5 goes out. I'm waiting on DeepSource's result (about four minutes) before bringing it to you for the merge.

**What the fix does:**
- An invite link never signs anyone in to an account that already exists. That person must already be signed in as themselves to join.
- If they aren't signed in, the invite page says "You already have a Proactive account. Sign in with your usual password to join Diggerman Dan", and signing in brings them back to the invite.
- Joining with an existing account no longer shows a "Create a password" box, which is what confused Scott.
- New people join exactly as before.

**1. Check prod for past misuse.** This lists every invite accepted for an account that already existed, before v0.2.5 went live. It only reads; it changes nothing. On the prod server, in `/opt/pbd/deploy`, paste this:

```
docker compose --env-file ../.env -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec -T postgres psql -U pbd -d pbd <<'SQL'
SELECT i.usedat AS accepted_at, i.email AS invitee, invitee.isddesadmin AS invitee_is_ddes_admin,
       t.entityname AS company, inviter.email AS invited_by, s.ip AS accepting_ip,
       left(s.useragent, 60) AS accepting_browser,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions s2 WHERE s2.userid = i.invitedbyuserid AND s2.ip = s.ip) AS same_ip_as_inviter
FROM memberinvitations i
JOIN users invitee ON lower(invitee.email) = lower(i.email)
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = i.tenantid
LEFT JOIN users inviter ON inviter.id = i.invitedbyuserid
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT ip, useragent FROM sessions WHERE userid = invitee.id
  AND createdat BETWEEN i.usedat - interval '1 minute' AND i.usedat + interval '1 minute'
  ORDER BY createdat LIMIT 1) s ON true
WHERE i.status = 'used' AND invitee.createdat < i.createdat
  AND i.usedat < timestamptz '2026-10-13 23:53:00+00'
ORDER BY i.usedat;
SQL
```

I'd expect to see Scott joining Darling Downs Earthmoving Solutions and Diggerman Dan. For any other row, `same_ip_as_inviter = t` means the browser that accepted the invite had also been used by the person who sent it. Paste me the results and I'll go through them with you.

PR #114 is merged, so `dev` now has the v0.2.5 fix and its screen tests.

Here's the spec draft for Scott's problem (`a883ca84`). Nothing is written to the spec files or coded until you approve it.

**Proposed: new SCOPE-003 FR-014, plus one line added to SCOPE-002 FR-002**

> ### FR-014 — Move between the Platform console and your own companies
>
> A DDES_ADMIN can also belong to companies, such as their own business or a customer they work with. They reach both without signing out or using a second account.
>
> **Acceptance Criteria**:
> - [ ] A DDES_ADMIN lands on the Platform console at sign-in and at `/`. They are never asked to pick a company first.
> - [ ] The console's account menu lists every company the person currently belongs to, as "Switch to <company>". Choosing one makes it their active company (SCOPE-002 FR-002) and opens that company's normal home for their role there.
> - [ ] Inside a company, the account menu shows "Platform console", which returns to `/admin`. This entry appears only for DDES_ADMINs.
> - [ ] Inside a company, the person sees and can do exactly what their roles in that company allow. Being a DDES_ADMIN adds nothing inside a company, and company roles add nothing in the console.
> - [ ] A DDES_ADMIN with no company memberships sees no "Switch to" entries.
> - [ ] The account keeps the admin session rules while working in a company: it ends after 1 hour of inactivity and "stay signed in" isn't offered (SCOPE-002 FR-004).

**SCOPE-002 FR-002, added line:**
> - [ ] A DDES_ADMIN is not asked to choose a company at sign-in. They land on the Platform console and switch from its account menu (SCOPE-003 FR-014).

**The decision inside this: Scott's company sessions keep the admin rules.** He'll be signed out after an hour of inactivity even while working in Darling Downs Earthmoving Solutions, and he can't tick "stay signed in". I've drafted it that way because his account can open the whole platform, and a long-lived session on his phone or a shared office computer would be a risk. The alternative is to give him normal company session rules while he's in a company and the strict rules only in the console. That's more complex, and it leaves a powerful account signed in for longer.

Shall I write this into the spec as drafted? If you approve, I'll build it through the usual flow: a branch off `dev`, tests, the DeepSource result to you, and a merge only on your OK.

**16:08 — Claude:**

I've found the cause, and nothing has been changed on either server. The scraper works on prod: it isn't blocked, and it pulled real machine specs. **Every model is then rejected when it's saved, because prod's equipment-type names don't match RitchieSpecs' names.**

**What happened on prod**, in the scheduled import on 12 Oct (480 models fetched, 0 imported):

| Why rejected | Models |
|---|---|
| Unknown equipment type "4wd Tractor" | 122 |
| Unknown equipment type "Forklift" | 120 |
| Unknown equipment type "Articulated Dump Truck" | 120 |
| "No usable record": old 2005 truck pages that no longer exist on the site (normal) | 118 |
| Unknown equipment type "Dump Truck" | 2 |

**Why the names don't match:**
- Prod has only DDES's own 26 working types, the prestart list (Excavator, Articulated Dump Truck (ADT), Loader and so on).
- RitchieSpecs uses its own names: Hydraulic Excavator, Mini Excavator, Articulated Dump Truck, Forklift, 4wd Tractor and about 50 more across the four industries you import.
- The importer needs an exact name match. It works on my local copy only because that database also has RitchieSpecs' names, added during development.
- The spec (SCOPE-013 FR-001) says the type list should "mirror Ritchie Specs' top layer", but prod was set up with DDES's prestart list instead.

**It also wastes time.** The importer only discovers a missing type after scraping each model page. Each run spends about 1.5 hours fetching pages it can never save, and every failure is reported with the same vague reason.

The dev server has the same gap (28 types, the same "4wd Tractor" failures), so we can test a fix there safely.

**Ways to fix it:**

1. **Map RitchieSpecs' types to DDES's (recommended).** In the console, against the RitchieSpecs source, you'd say where each of their types belongs: "Articulated Dump Truck" goes under "Articulated Dump Truck (ADT)"; "Hydraulic", "Mini" and "Midi Excavator" all go under "Excavator"; "Forklift" either gets a new DDES type or is skipped.
   - Imported models land in DDES's own types, so they line up with your prestart templates.
   - Before scraping, the importer would check the mapping and skip any type that isn't mapped. It would show those in the console as "needs mapping", rather than spending an hour and a half failing.
   - This is a new feature, so I'd write the spec change for your approval first (SCOPE-032 plus a small new table).
2. **Add RitchieSpecs' names to the type list.** This needs no code: you add them in Admin → Equipment → Types & makes, then re-run. But you'd end up with near-duplicates, such as "Articulated Dump Truck" next to "Articulated Dump Truck (ADT)", and prestart templates keyed to DDES's names wouldn't apply to imported models.
3. **Rename DDES's types to RitchieSpecs' names.** I wouldn't recommend this, because it changes names your prestart setup already depends on.

Whichever you choose, I'd also fix two smaller things:
- record the real reason against each failed model, instead of the same vague message;
- stop the old truck pages from eating each run's page budget.

Which way would you like to go? If it's option 1, I'll draft the spec change, starting with a proposed mapping of RitchieSpecs' types onto your 26.

**The draft change below needs your approval before I write it into the specs or build anything.** It follows your approach, with three additions that make it work smoothly:
1. **The import adds RitchieSpecs' types itself.** That covers today's 44 and any new type they add later, so nobody types them in by hand.
2. **These types stay out of everyone else's way.** Without this, tenants, prestart and fleet would see 70 near-duplicate types.

> **SCOPE-013 FR-001 — amendment (equipment types)**
> - [ ] Each type is either a **DDES type** (the platform's working list, offered to tenants, prestart templates and fleet) or a **source type** (a catalogue source's own name, such as RitchieSpecs' "Hydraulic Excavator").
> - [ ] Source types appear only in the catalogue admin. Tenants, prestart and fleet never offer them.
>
> **SCOPE-032 new FR — file imported models under DDES types at approval**
> - [ ] Each imported model comes in under the source's own type name, exactly as RitchieSpecs has it. A missing name is added to the type list automatically, as a source type.
> - [ ] To approve an imported candidate, the approver chooses which DDES type it is filed under ("File under"). Approving moves it to that type and publishes it.
> - [ ] The choice is remembered for each source type and pre-filled for the next candidate of that type. For example, after you file one "Hydraulic Excavator" under "Excavator", the next one is already set to "Excavator". The approver can always change it.
> - [ ] A later import recognises a machine already in the catalogue by its RitchieSpecs page, so a model filed under a DDES type never comes back as a new candidate.
> - [ ] A model that fails to import records the real reason, such as "page no longer exists", "blocked" or "no specs on the page", not one vague message.

1. Build it, with tests, on a branch.

**17:39 — Claude:**

The old "ingest" endpoint only takes whole categories, so a single-URL import would be new. Here's the draft spec change for your approval. Nothing will be built until you approve it.

> **SCOPE-032 new FR-017 — Import one model from its RitchieSpecs page**
>
> A DDES admin can add a specific machine that the scheduled imports haven't reached, by pasting its RitchieSpecs page link.
>
> **Acceptance Criteria**:
> - [ ] The Scrape jobs screen has an **"Import one model"** box: paste a RitchieSpecs model link (e.g. `https://www.ritchiespecs.com/model/caterpillar-320-hydraulic-excavator`), then press Import.
> - [ ] Only RitchieSpecs model pages are accepted. Any other site or page is refused with a plain message, and nothing is fetched. A trailing slash, `www` or a query string is tidied up first.
> - [ ] If the machine is **already in the catalogue** (matched by its RitchieSpecs page, rejected models excepted), nothing is fetched. The admin sees "Already in the catalogue: <make model> (<status>)" with a link to it.
> - [ ] Otherwise that one page is scraped straight away and saved as a **candidate**, never published, under RitchieSpecs' own type. A missing type name is added as a source type in its RitchieSpecs industry (FR-016). It then goes through the normal approval, including "File under".
> - [ ] Only machines in the source's **cleared industries** can be imported (today: Agriculture, Construction, Lifting & Material Handling, Transportation). Anything else is refused with "That model is in <industry>, which isn't cleared for RitchieSpecs." The licence boundary is never crossed by a pasted link.
> - [ ] The admin sees the outcome on the spot: "Added <make model> as a candidate", with a link to review it, or the plain reason it failed (FR-016 reasons, such as "Page no longer exists").
> - [ ] Each attempt is recorded in the run log as a one-item run marked "single page". It is audited (FR-013) and retained like any run (FR-014).
> - [ ] DDES admins only (FR-012).

**The decision inside this:** I've limited pasted links to the industries already cleared for RitchieSpecs, so nobody can step outside the licence boundary by pasting a link. The cost is that a Forestry or Asphalt machine can't be added this way until that industry is cleared for the source. Do you want that limit, or should any RitchieSpecs model be importable?

**How it works underneath:** it reuses this week's import code: the same scraper, the same source-type and "File under" rules, the same "already have it" check by page, and the same failure reasons. It's a small addition, not a new system, and needs no database change.

Shall I write this into the spec and build it?

## Draft for approval: SCOPE-029 clock-in duplicate check (card 9e6ff9f0)

**The problem:** The database blocks the same offline clock-in id twice across all companies and all workers. The app now checks for a repeat clock-in per company and per worker (PR #126), so the database rule is wider than what the app checks. If two different workers' phones ever produce the same id, the second sync fails with a raw database error.

### 1. Scope doc: `specs/Project-Scope/029-rostering-time-clock.md`, Data Model, the `timeentries` row

The last column (Relationships / constraints) changes to:

> `userid`→users; `projectid`→projects(028); `rostershiftid`→rostershifts; `verificationphotokey`→SCOPE-014; **partial `unique(tenantid, userid) where clockoutat is null`** (one open clock-in per worker **per tenant**, tenant-scoped, consistent with FR-012); **partial `unique(tenantid, userid, clientgeneratedid) where clientgeneratedid is not null`** (once-only offline sync is deduped **per worker per tenant**, so one worker's device id can never block, clash with or return another worker's or another company's entry) *(amended 2026-10-18, card `9e6ff9f0`: was a global `unique(clientgeneratedid)`)*; check `clockoutat >= clockinat`. *(No geofence-enforcement column in Alpha. Lat/lng is captured for map display; geofence is deferred.)*

### 2. Scope doc: FR-003, the offline acceptance line

> - [ ] **Offline-first**: events are written to on-device SQLite continuously, then pushed, and the local copy is cleared only when the server confirms. Sync is **once-only**: it is deduped on `clientgeneratedid` **for the same worker in the same company**. A re-sent event comes back as the entry that already exists, never as an error or a second entry. Another worker's identical id is treated as a separate event and never returns someone else's entry. GPS and timestamp are captured at event time, not sync time. *(Built against the **platform `offline-sync` shared module**; see the Notes ownership decision. It is extracted and built here in FR-003, and 017 migrates to it opportunistically. Task `dc6fee8c`.)*

### 3. Spec: `specs/029-*/spec.md`, the `timeentries` sentence in the data model

Inside the `timeentries (...)` list, `partial unique(userid) where clockoutat is null; unique(clientgeneratedid);` becomes:

> `partial unique(tenantid,userid) where clockoutat is null; partial unique(tenantid,userid,clientgeneratedid) where clientgeneratedid is not null;`

This also fixes a stale entry: spec.md still says the open-clock-in rule is per worker only, while the scope doc already says per worker per company.

- **Schema:** replace `timeentries_clientid_uq` with `timeentries_tenant_user_clientid_uq` on (tenantid, userid, clientgeneratedid), keeping the "not null" filter. I'll generate a drizzle migration with `db:generate` and run it locally with `db:migrate`.
  - Existing data can't break the migration, because the new rule only allows more combinations than the old one.
- **Service (`timeclock.ts`):** if two copies of the same sync arrive at the same moment and the database rejects one as a duplicate, return the existing entry instead of an error, which keeps the "once-only" promise. Nothing new is shown to the user.
- **Tests:** another worker's identical id gets its own entry; a simultaneous duplicate returns the existing entry; plus mutation checks.
- **Process:** the standard steps, from the card going in_progress through to a PR into dev and the DeepSource result reported to you.

**FR-001 — Roster / scheduling**
> Create/edit/publish shifts with templates, open shifts and multi-view scheduling.
> - [ ] Shift = worker (or **Unassigned/open**) + optional SCOPE-028 Project / SCOPE-016 depot + date + start/end + optional SCOPE-010 job title + break plan; lifecycle `DRAFT → PUBLISHED → CONFIRMED → OPEN → SWAP_IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED`. **An end time earlier than the start time means the shift ends the next day (an overnight shift). > - [ ] Views by location/crew/role/individual in day/week/fortnight; templates (single/daily/weekly) storing break plan + required quals; duplicate-a-week; drag-drop.

> - [ ] **Who can do what: create, edit and publish need `manage-roster`. Cancelling a shift needs `manage-roster` or `supervise-roster`. A cancellation notifies the affected worker (SCOPE-025) and is audited (FR-011).**

  - 0% pixel change on the screenshots, or any tiny difference explained;
  - all tests pass;
  - a click-through per role, including an open dialog, shows no layout break.
- **One question: older browsers.** Tailwind 4 needs Safari 16.4 or newer (iPhones on iOS 16.4+), Chrome 111+ and Firefox 128+. On older browsers some styling is lost. The kit's top-level `--help` prints help, but `dbpush --help` ignored the flag and pushed all 24 local spec folders. The push:
- **Didn't change:** any task, task status, spec status or stage. Nothing appears to be lost.
- **Created about 45 extra documents:** copies of "Spec / Plan / Tests" for most specs. Their titles don't match the originals, so the originals are untouched and you now have two copies of many specs. This is also where the old duplicate "Spec 011/012" documents came from.
- **Overwrote about 20 existing documents** with the local versions:
  - for 002, 003, 007, 014 and 015, the plans (the wxKanban ones were near-empty);
  - for 011 and 012, spec, plan and tests;
  - for 016, 033 and 036, spec and plan.

  For all but 011 and 012, the local copy was the same age or newer. For 011 and 012, wxKanban's copies were dated one day after the local files. It was most likely the same content pushed again, but I can't prove it.

I've logged it as an event in wxKanban and added a memory rule: never run a kit command just to see its help, and always run `dbpush --dry-run` first.

**11:45 — Claude:**

I'm still working. Surface 1 of 20, **Authentication & sessions**, is done and saved to `.review-progress.json`.

**Result: 3 must-fix, 18 should-fix, 5 nit.** Every one already exists on `dev`; none came from today. Full report: [01-auth-sessions.md](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrewmathiesonblakely-Projects-Proactive-By-DDES/45e53ca3-6e2d-4e1a-b5a3-5d84571035df/scratchpad/review/01-auth-sessions.md)

**Must-fix**
1. **Sign-in slowdown and reset limit apply to everyone at once.** The API doesn't trust the Caddy proxy, so every user looks like the same visitor.
   - After 20 failed sign-ins anywhere, *everyone's* sign-in slows by up to 15 seconds.
   - After 10 reset requests platform-wide, nobody receives a reset email, but the page still says one is on its way.
   - One attacker could keep this going indefinitely.
   - The fix is one line in `index.ts`: `app.set("trust proxy", 1)`.
2. **After a password reset or change, the user loses their company.** Their menu empties and a Tenant Admin is sent to the worker home (`password.ts:58`, `:114`).

**Worth knowing from the should-fix list**
- The "Keep me signed in for 30 days" box is ticked by default, though the spec says opt-in.
- If sign-out fails, the screen still shows signed out, but the 30-day session survives on shared tablets.
- With no company chosen, a user who belongs to several companies can end up acting in an arbitrary one.
- Single-use reset and verification links can be used twice at the same moment.
- Session expiry doesn't send the user back to sign-in.

**Affects every surface:** the test stand-in for the database ignores filters and constraints, so tests can't prove tenant isolation. A small real-Postgres test tier would close that.
